title: International health agencies and global goals

steps.tx: The **World Health Organization** (WHO) is the directing and coordinating authority for international health within the United Nations system. Its headquarters is in **Geneva**, Switzerland. The South East Asia Regional Office (SEARO) is in New Delhi, India, and covers 11 member countries. WHO was constituted on 7 April 1948, which is marked each year as World Health Day.
steps.say: The World Health Organization is the directing and coordinating authority for international health within the United Nations system. Its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland. The South East Asia Regional Office is in New Delhi, India, and covers eleven member countries. WHO came into force on 7 April 1948, and that date is marked every year as World Health Day.

steps.tx: Other United Nations health-related agencies have their own seats. **UNICEF**, founded in 1946 for children in war-affected countries, is based in New York. The **FAO** is in Rome, the **ILO** in Geneva, and **UNESCO** in Paris. UNFPA and UNDP are also UN agencies that work on population and development. Knowing where each agency sits is a common recall question.

steps.tx: The **Millennium Development Goals** (MDGs) were eight goals adopted at the UN Millennium Summit in September 2000, with 1990 as the baseline and **2015** as the target year. Three goals were directly health related: child mortality (goal 4), maternal health (goal 5) and combating HIV/AIDS, malaria and other diseases (goal 6). Under goal 4 the under-five mortality rate was to fall by two-thirds, and under goal 5 the maternal mortality ratio was to fall by three-quarters.

steps.tx: UNICEF and WHO launched the **Baby Friendly Hospital Initiative** (BFHI) in 1992 to protect and promote breastfeeding. UNICEF also promotes the **GOBI-FFF** strategy: growth monitoring, oral rehydration, breastfeeding, immunisation, plus family planning, female education and food supplementation. In GOBI, the O stands for oral rehydration, not oral contraceptives.
